title: Structured leakage in OAM-encoded qubits revealed by distributed quantum feature extraction
authors: Yayu Mo, Nazifa Rumman, Sanjeev Shapkota, Thomas A. Searles, Sanjaya Lohani
abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes have emerged as an important platform for high-dimensional quantum communication but remain vulnerable to environmental noise and channel imperfections. Here we introduce a logical-qubit representation of OAM propagation in which modes evolve as qubits through noisy quantum channels. In this representation, turbulence manifests as leakage from the logical OAM subspace into turbulence-induced leakage components, providing a unified description of degradation in both single-photon and coherent-beam regimes. We show that turbulence-induced leakage exhibits systematic dependence on turbulence strength and OAM order, revealing structured signatures of information redistribution beyond the logical subspace. Leveraging this insight, we develop a distributed quantum feature-extraction scheme that encodes high-dimensional OAM states into quantum representations and employs quantum convolutional operations to extract turbulence-robust features. Simulations and experimental measurements demonstrate robust extraction of these features across a broad range of turbulence strengths, OAM orders, and propagation conditions. Our results establish a direct link between OAM-channel dynamics, structured leakage, and quantum learning, providing a physics-informed framework for characterizing turbulence-degraded high-dimensional optical states and extracting robust signatures of turbulence-induced information redistribution.
summary: This research tackles the challenge of noise in OAM-encoded quantum communication by modeling turbulence-induced degradation as structured leakage. The authors propose and validate a novel distributed quantum feature-extraction technique that uses quantum convolutional operations to extract robust signatures of this structured leakage, linking channel dynamics directly to quantum machine learning principles.
main_problem: The paper addresses the vulnerability of Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM)-encoded qubits to environmental noise, specifically atmospheric turbulence, and seeks to characterize the structured information loss beyond the ideal quantum subspace.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that turbulence causes structured leakage, which can be robustly extracted using a novel distributed quantum feature-extraction scheme employing quantum convolutional operations.
method: The methodology combines theoretical modeling of OAM propagation through noisy channels with experimental validation using controlled turbulence and quantum convolutional processing.
model_or_system: The system uses OAM modes for high-dimensional quantum communication, modeled as logical qubits propagating through channels characterized by turbulence (Kolmogorov phase screens). The analysis employs a logical-qubit representation and quantum convolutional operations (QConv) for feature extraction.
key_observables: Structured leakage magnitude, Quantum-State Fidelity, Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), and the evolution of the scattering matrix.
important_parameters: Turbulence strength (quantified by Strehl Ratio, SR), OAM order ($\ell$), and the size of the simulated OAM basis ($\ell_{	ext{max}}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the structured leakage signatures are physically meaningful and can be captured by mapping intensity distributions into quantum feature spaces, requiring the use of an erasure operator to maintain trace-preservation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the overall pipeline (simulation/experiment/QConv), the evolution of the scattering matrix showing leakage trends with turbulence, and comparisons between reconstructed states under various noise models.
paper_structure: The paper establishes a framework by modeling OAM propagation through noisy channels, quantifying structured leakage via the scattering matrix, and then developing a distributed quantum feature-extraction scheme using QConv to robustly extract these leakage-related signatures.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges quantum optics (OAM modes, turbulence) with quantum information processing (feature extraction, robust encoding), providing a physics-informed method to characterize decoherence in high-dimensional photonic quantum channels.
